items.stem: What is meant by "Corporate social responsibility"?
items.answer: Voluntary activities of a company that contribute to the well-being of society beyond what law requires.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Voluntary activities of a company that contribute to the well-being of society beyond what law requires.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the arguments against social responsibility?
items.answer: Avoidance of government regulation
items.markingKey: (a) "Avoidance of government regulation" is one of the arguments for social responsibility, not one of the arguments against social responsibility.

items.stem: Distinguish between social responsibility and legal responsibility on the basis of scope, basis and consequence of non-fulfilment.
items.answer: (i) Scope: social responsibility: wider: includes legal and moral obligations; legal responsibility: narrower: only what law requires. (ii) Basis: social responsibility: values and expectations of society; legal responsibility: laws passed by the government. (iii) Consequence of non-fulfilment: social responsibility: loss of goodwill and public image; legal responsibility: legal penalty or punishment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Scope: social responsibility: wider: includes legal and moral obligations; legal responsibility: narrower: only what law requires. (ii) Basis: social responsibility: values and expectations of society; legal responsibility: laws passed by the government. (iii) Consequence of non-fulfilment: social responsibility: loss of goodwill and public image; legal responsibility: legal penalty or punishment.

items.stem: A shareholder argues that managers of Malhotra Brothers are trained in business, not in solving social problems. Which argument about social responsibility is it?
items.answer: Lack of social skills
items.markingKey: (d) Lack of social skills. Business people lack skills for social problems.

items.stem: Rao and Sons turns farm waste into packaging material and sells it at a profit. Which argument about social responsibility is it? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Converting problems into opportunities. A social problem becomes a business opportunity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Converting problems into opportunities; 2 marks for the justification: A social problem becomes a business opportunity.

items.stem:
At the annual meeting of Mishra Brothers, one shareholder says spending on a school for workers' children is a waste of profit. The chairperson replies that it will help the company in the long run.
(i) Give the argument used by the shareholder and one by the chairperson. (ii) Give one more argument the chairperson could use.
items.answer: (i) Shareholder: violation of profit maximisation objective. Chairperson: long-term interest of the firm. (ii) Better environment for business, maintenance of society, availability of resources with business (any one).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Shareholder: violation of profit maximisation objective. Chairperson: long-term interest of the firm. (ii) Better environment for business, maintenance of society, availability of resources with business (any one).

items.stem:
A government plans strict new rules after several factories near Dehradun ignored public complaints. Kulkarni Brothers instead voluntarily sets up a waste treatment plant and helps clean the river.
(i) Is Kulkarni Brothers's action legal or social responsibility? Why? (ii) Which argument for social responsibility does it show? (iii) State two arguments against such actions.
items.answer: (i) Social responsibility: it is voluntary, beyond what the law required at the time. (ii) Avoidance of government regulation (also holding business responsible for problems it caused). (iii) Burden on consumers, violation of profit maximisation, lack of social skills (any two).
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Social responsibility: it is voluntary, beyond what the law required at the time. (ii) Avoidance of government regulation (also holding business responsible for problems it caused). (iii) Burden on consumers, violation of profit maximisation, lack of social skills (any two).

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the arguments for social responsibility?
items.answer: Converting problems into opportunities
items.markingKey: (a) "Converting problems into opportunities" is one of the arguments for social responsibility; the others are arguments against social responsibility.

items.stem: A critic says the cost of Kapoor Agencies's social schemes will only raise the price of its handicrafts. Which argument about social responsibility is it?
items.answer: Burden on consumers
items.markingKey: (a) Burden on consumers. Costs are passed on to consumers.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Discretionary responsibility"?
items.answer: Purely voluntary obligations such as charitable contributions to educational institutions or flood relief.
items.markingKey: (b) Discretionary responsibility: Purely voluntary obligations such as charitable contributions to educational institutions or flood relief.
options: The responsibility to behave in ways society expects even if the law does not require it.
Purely voluntary obligations such as charitable contributions to educational institutions or flood relief.
The responsibility of a business to obey the laws of the land.
The responsibility of a business to produce goods and services that society wants and sell them at a profit.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the responsibilities of business towards workers?
items.answer: Proper after-sales service
items.markingKey: (b) "Proper after-sales service" is one of the responsibilities of business towards consumers, not one of the responsibilities of business towards workers.

items.stem: Explain the following kinds of social responsibility: (i) Legal responsibility (ii) Economic responsibility.
items.answer: (i) Legal responsibility: Obey the laws of the land. (ii) Economic responsibility: Produce goods and services society wants and sell them at a profit.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Obey the laws of the land. (ii) Produce goods and services society wants and sell them at a profit.

items.stem: Pillai Retail withdraws an advertisement that hurt the religious feelings of a community, though no law required it. Which kind of social responsibility is shown?
items.answer: Ethical responsibility
items.markingKey: (d) Ethical responsibility. Morally right behaviour beyond law.

items.stem: Singh Enterprises follows the rules on minimum wages set by law. Which kind of social responsibility is shown? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Legal responsibility. Following law is legal responsibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Legal responsibility; 2 marks for the justification: Following law is legal responsibility.

items.stem: Which kind of social responsibility is shown? In each case give a reason. (i) Mehta Retail pays all its taxes on time and follows labour laws. (ii) Mehta Retail withdraws an advertisement that hurt the religious feelings of a community, though no law required it.
items.answer: (i) Legal responsibility: Obeying the law is legal responsibility. (ii) Ethical responsibility: Morally right behaviour beyond law.

items.stem: State any three steps business can take to protect the environment.

items.stem: Explain the following examples of unethical business practices: (i) Black marketing and hoarding (ii) Misleading advertisements.

(iii) Basis: social responsibility: values and expectations of society; legal responsibility: laws passed by the government. (iv) Consequence of non-fulfilment: social responsibility: loss of goodwill and public image; legal responsibility: legal penalty or punishment.

items.stem:
Goyal Enterprises of Kochi pays fair wages, pays taxes on time, avoids misleading advertisements and sponsors a free eye camp every year.
(i) Identify the interest groups served by each action. (ii) Which kind of responsibility is the eye camp?
items.answer: (i) Fair wages: workers; taxes: government; honest ads: consumers; eye camp: community. (ii) Discretionary responsibility.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Fair wages: workers; taxes: government; honest ads: consumers; eye camp: community. (ii) Discretionary responsibility.

items.stem: Plastic and industrial waste from Bose Stores is buried in fields near Jaipur. Which type of pollution is caused?
items.answer: Land pollution
items.markingKey: (d) Land pollution. Waste dumped on land.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about business ethics is NOT correct?
items.answer: Business ethics are the same as the laws of the land.
items.markingKey: (b) Incorrect statement: Business ethics are the same as the laws of the land.
